plan_a_advantages: Low risk of injury due to easy pace
plan_b_advantages: Includes a longer, controlled effort run
Addresses both aerobic endurance and threshold strength
reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. While Plan A focuses solely on easy runs, which is beneficial for building a base, it lacks any structured intensity work. Plan B incorporates a tempo run and a longer, controlled effort, directly addressing the need to improve speed and threshold strength – key components for trail running performance. Furthermore, the inclusion of a longer run at an easy pace is crucial for building the endurance required for longer trail races, something absent in Plan A. Plan A’s repetitive easy runs could lead to plateaus, whereas Plan B provides a more progressive and challenging stimulus.
